definition: A model-compression approach that represents model weights or other numerical values using 4-bit precision, substantially reducing memory requirements while potentially changing accuracy or performance.

definition: The broad field of creating machine-based systems that can perform tasks associated with human intelligence, such as perception, learning, reasoning, language use, decision-making, or goal-directed action.

definition: A neural-network mechanism that lets a model assign different importance to different parts of its input when producing a representation or output.

definition: An AI capability that allows a model or agent to interact with a computer interface by interpreting the screen and taking actions such as moving a pointer, clicking, and typing.

definition: Cryptographically verifiable provenance information attached to or associated with digital content to record claims about its origin, edits, and processing history using the C2PA standard.

definition: A technique for reusing computation associated with previously processed context so repeated or shared prompt prefixes do not have to be fully recomputed for every generation.

definition: The practice of selecting, organizing, maintaining, and refreshing the information available in a model's context so it has the right instructions, data, tools, history, and state for a task.

definition: The tendency for a language model's ability to use relevant information reliably to decline as the amount of context grows, even when the needed information remains inside the context window.

definition: The amount of information an AI model can actively consider during an interaction, including instructions, conversation history, documents, and other supplied information.

definition: An AI assistant designed to work alongside a person by suggesting, drafting, analyzing, summarizing, or completing portions of a task while the human remains responsible for the work.

definition: A measure of how closely two vectors point in the same direction, calculated from the cosine of the angle between them.

definition: A form of machine learning that uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn increasingly complex representations from data.

definition: AI-generated or AI-manipulated image, audio, or video that realistically imitates a person, object, place, or event in a way that can falsely appear authentic.

definition: A Chinese artificial intelligence research organization that develops and publishes the DeepSeek family of language and reasoning models and operates DeepSeek web, app, and API services.

definition: A post-training method that fine-tunes a language model directly on preferred and rejected response pairs without first training a separate explicit reward model.

definition: A model-compression and transfer technique in which a smaller or simpler model is trained to reproduce useful behavior or knowledge from a larger model or ensemble.

definition: Running a trained AI model to make predictions or generate outputs on computing infrastructure near the data source or end device rather than sending the workload to a distant centralized cloud service.

definition: A numerical representation of data in a vector space where items with similar meaning or characteristics can be positioned near one another.
example: The system converted each paragraph into an embedding so it could find passages with similar meaning.

definition: A structured evaluation used to measure whether an AI model or system meets specified performance, quality, safety, or reliability criteria.

definition: Further training a pretrained AI model on additional task-specific or domain-specific data so its behavior becomes better suited to a particular purpose.

definition: A broadly trained AI model that can be adapted to many downstream tasks rather than being built for only one narrow purpose.

definition: Artificial intelligence that creates new content such as text, images, audio, video, code, or other data based on patterns learned from existing data.

definition: An evaluation metric estimating whether at least one successful solution appears among k independently sampled model outputs for the same task, commonly used in code-generation evaluation.
example: The coding benchmark reported pass@10 because the model was allowed ten sampled attempts at each problem.

definition: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning, a family of techniques that adapt pretrained models by training only a relatively small subset of parameters or added components instead of updating the full model.
example: PEFT made it practical to maintain several specialized adaptations without storing a complete fine-tuned model for each task.

definition: The initial training phase in which a model learns broad patterns from a large dataset before being adapted or fine-tuned for more specific tasks.
example: The model learned general language patterns during pretraining before it was fine-tuned for customer support.

definition: Input given to a generative AI model to guide what it should do, how it should respond, or what context it should use.
example: The prompt asked the model to summarize the report for a nontechnical audience.

definition: Reusing previously processed prompt or context tokens so repeated model requests can be handled with lower latency, lower cost, or both.
example: Prompt caching reduced the cost of repeatedly sending the same long system instructions with every API request.

definition: A workflow that uses the output from one prompt as input or context for a later prompt so a larger task can be completed in stages.
example: The workflow used prompt chaining to extract facts first, evaluate them second, and draft the final summary last.

definition: The practice of structuring instructions, examples, context, constraints, and workflows so an AI system can produce useful and reliable results.
example: Good prompt engineering is less about magic words and more about clearly defining the task.

definition: An attempt to manipulate an AI system by embedding instructions in content that interfere with or override the system's intended instructions.
example: The webpage contained a prompt injection attempting to convince the assistant to disregard its original task.

definition: A reusable prompt structure containing placeholders or variables that can be replaced with different values for repeated or programmatic use.
example: The team used one prompt template and substituted the customer name, product, and support issue for each request.

definition: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique that keeps a pretrained model quantized, commonly at 4-bit precision, while training low-rank adapter weights instead of updating the full model.
example: The team used QLoRA to fine-tune a large model on a single workstation with much lower memory requirements.

definition: Reducing the numerical precision used to represent a model's weights or computations, usually to lower memory use and improve inference efficiency.
example: Quantization reduced the model's memory footprint enough to run it on a smaller device.

definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, a method in which an AI retrieves relevant information from external sources and provides it to a language model when generating a response.
example: The assistant uses RAG to retrieve our company standards before answering questions about them.

definition: The evaluation of a retrieval-augmented generation system across retrieval and answer quality, using measures such as relevance, groundedness, completeness, correctness, retrieval quality, or end-to-end task performance.
example: The team ran RAG evaluation before launch to test whether the retriever found useful context and whether answers stayed grounded in it.

definition: A configurable setting that controls how much reasoning computation a supported AI model uses before producing an answer, allowing developers or users to trade off response quality, latency, and token use.
example: The developer increased reasoning effort for the harder analysis task and lowered it for simple retrieval requests.

definition: An AI model optimized to perform more extensive multi-step analysis before producing an answer, particularly for problems involving logic, planning, mathematics, coding, or complex decisions.
example: We used a reasoning model because the problem required several dependent calculations.

definition: A rank-fusion method that combines multiple ranked result lists by assigning each result a score based on its reciprocal rank in each list and summing those contributions into one final ranking.
example: The search system used reciprocal rank fusion to combine keyword and vector retrieval results without directly comparing their raw relevance scores.

definition: Adversarial testing in which people or systems deliberately probe an AI system for harmful capabilities, weaknesses, unsafe behavior, or ways to bypass its safeguards.
example: External red teaming found several jailbreak paths that the development team addressed before release.

definition: A machine-learning approach in which an agent learns behavior by taking actions and receiving rewards or penalties based on their outcomes.
example: The robot used reinforcement learning to improve its policy through repeated interaction with the environment.

definition: A model or component that takes an existing set of retrieved candidates and reorders them according to their estimated relevance to a query or task.
example: The search pipeline used a reranker after retrieval to move the most relevant documents to the top of the context.

definition: Reordering an initial set of search or retrieval results using an additional relevance model so the most useful results appear first.
example: Reranking moved the policy paragraph that directly answered the question above several loosely related search results.

definition: An approach to designing, developing, deploying, and governing AI with explicit attention to trustworthiness and societal impacts such as fairness, safety, privacy, transparency, accountability, and human oversight.
example: The organization's responsible AI program requires risk review, documentation, human oversight, and monitoring before high-impact systems are deployed.

definition: The process of finding and returning information that is relevant to a query from a search index, database, knowledge source, or other collection.
example: The assistant used retrieval to find the three policy sections most relevant to the employee's question.

definition: A model trained to score or rank outputs according to preferences or desired behavior, providing a reward signal that can guide further model training.
example: The reward model ranked two candidate responses so the training system could favor the one judged more helpful.

definition: Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback, a training approach in which feedback or preferences generated by AI systems are used to create a reward signal for reinforcement learning.
example: The experiment used RLAIF so an AI preference model, rather than only human raters, helped shape the assistant's behavior.

definition: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, a training approach that uses human preferences or evaluations to help shape a model's behavior toward desired responses.
example: The model underwent RLHF so human preference data could influence which kinds of responses it learned to favor.

definition: A tensor serialization format designed to store model weights and other tensors safely and efficiently without relying on executable pickle-based serialization.
example: The model repository provided Safetensors weights so the runtime could load the checkpoint without using a pickle file.

definition: The systematic testing of an AI model or system for safety-relevant behaviors, risks, safeguards, and failure modes under defined conditions or scenarios.
example: The release process included safety evaluation for harmful compliance, refusal behavior, and agent actions before deployment.

definition: A generation method in which an AI model selects among possible next tokens according to a probability distribution rather than always choosing only the single highest-probability option.
example: Using sampling instead of greedy decoding produced more varied responses from the language model.

definition: An attention mechanism in which elements within the same input sequence compare with one another so the model can represent how those elements relate in context.
example: Self-attention helps a transformer determine which earlier words are most relevant to the word it is processing now.

definition: A learning approach that creates training targets from the structure of unlabeled data itself, allowing models to learn useful representations without manually supplied labels for every example.
example: The language model used self-supervised learning by predicting hidden or next tokens from raw text.

definition: A search approach that tries to match the meaning and intent of a query rather than relying only on exact keywords.
example: Semantic search found the policy even though the question used different wording from the document.

definition: The use of AI tools inside an organization without formal approval, governance, oversight, or sometimes the knowledge of its IT or security teams.
example: Employees entering company information into personal AI accounts created a shadow AI problem.

definition: A search method that returns items most similar to a query according to a chosen distance or similarity measure.
example: Similarity search returned passages whose embeddings were closest to the user's query.

definition: A language model designed with a smaller parameter count and computational footprint than large language models, often making it more practical for local, edge, or resource-constrained use.
example: The application uses a small language model on the device so basic requests can be processed without a cloud connection.

definition: An inference technique that speeds generation by having a faster helper produce candidate tokens that a larger model verifies in fewer expensive forward passes.
example: The serving stack used speculative decoding to reduce generation latency without changing the final model.

definition: An AI speech-recognition capability that converts spoken audio into written text or a text transcription.
example: The meeting assistant used speech-to-text to turn the recorded conversation into a searchable transcript.

definition: Model-generated output constrained to follow a specified machine-readable structure or schema so downstream software can reliably parse and use it.
example: The application requested structured output matching a JSON schema instead of free-form text.

definition: A specialized AI agent or agent-like worker delegated a narrower task by a primary agent or orchestration process, often with its own context, instructions, tools, or permissions.
example: The coding agent delegated repository exploration to a subagent and used the returned summary in the main task.

definition: Fine-tuning a pretrained model on labeled examples of desired inputs and outputs so its behavior better matches a target task or response style.
example: The team used supervised fine-tuning on curated question-and-answer pairs before applying preference-based training.

definition: A machine-learning approach in which a model learns from examples paired with known labels or target outputs.
example: The classifier used supervised learning from emails labeled as spam or not spam.

definition: Text, images, audio, video, data, or other media created wholly or substantially using artificial intelligence.
example: The organization requires synthetic content to be identified before publication.

definition: Artificially generated data designed to resemble or reproduce useful characteristics of real data and used for testing, simulation, privacy protection, or model training.
example: The team supplemented scarce real examples with synthetic data generated to represent additional scenarios.

definition: A document published about an AI system or major model release that summarizes evaluations, identified risks, safety measures, limitations, and other information relevant to understanding how the system was assessed and deployed.
example: The release included a system card describing safety evaluations, observed risks, and the safeguards used before deployment.

definition: A set of application-level instructions supplied to a generative AI system to establish behavior, constraints, context, or priorities before the user's request is processed.
example: The application uses a system prompt to define the assistant's role, formatting rules, and boundaries.

definition: A sampling setting that influences how predictable or varied a model's generated output is by changing how strongly it favors higher-probability next tokens.
example: Lowering the temperature made the model's responses more consistent, while a higher setting produced more varied wording.

definition: A generative AI capability that creates images from natural-language descriptions or prompts.
example: The designer used a text-to-image model to generate several concept illustrations from a written brief.

definition: An AI speech-synthesis capability that converts written text into spoken audio, often using generated voices.
example: The accessibility feature used text-to-speech to read the generated answer aloud.

definition: A generative AI task or model capability that creates video from a text prompt or description.
example: The creative team used a text-to-video model to generate a short scene from a written prompt.

definition: A small unit of text processed by a language model. A token may represent an entire word, part of a word, punctuation, or another portion of text.
example: Large documents consume more tokens and therefore more of the available context window.

definition: The process of converting text or other input into tokens that a model can represent and process, often by splitting text into words, subwords, characters, bytes, or other learned units and mapping them to token IDs.
example: Different tokenization methods can split the same sentence into different numbers and kinds of tokens.

definition: A human or policy-controlled checkpoint that must authorize an AI system or agent before it invokes a particular tool or performs a tool-mediated action.
example: The assistant paused for tool approval before allowing the connected service to modify production data.

definition: The ability of an AI model to request the use of an external function, application, database, search system, calculator, or other tool to complete a task.
example: Through tool calling, the assistant can check the database instead of trying to answer from memory.

definition: A sampling method that limits the next-token choices to the smallest set of likely tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a chosen threshold p, then samples from that set.
example: Lowering top-p narrowed the set of tokens the model considered during generation.

definition: The examples, text, images, audio, labels, or other information used to teach a machine-learning model during training.
example: The quality and composition of the training data can strongly influence what a model learns and how it behaves.

definition: Using knowledge learned for one task, domain, or dataset to improve learning or performance on another related task or domain.
example: Transfer learning let the team start from a pretrained model instead of training a new vision system from scratch.

definition: A neural-network architecture built around attention mechanisms that can process relationships among pieces of a sequence in parallel and underlies many modern language and multimodal models.
example: Most current large language models are based on the transformer architecture.

definition: A training failure in which a model does not capture enough of the structure or complexity in the training data to make useful predictions.
example: The model was underfitting because it performed poorly even on the examples it had been trained on.

definition: A machine-learning approach that trains on data without supplied target labels in order to discover patterns, structure, groupings, or useful representations.
example: The team used unsupervised learning to find clusters in customer behavior without predefined category labels.

definition: A prompt or message supplied with the user role, representing the end user's request, question, instruction, or additional context for the model.
example: The developer instructions stayed fixed while each customer's user prompt changed with the question they asked.

definition: A database designed to store, index, and search vector representations such as embeddings, often by finding items that are mathematically similar to a query vector.
example: The RAG system stores document embeddings in a vector database so it can retrieve relevant passages quickly.

definition: A search method that compares vector representations of data to find items that are close to a query in embedding space.
example: The application used vector search to find documents that were semantically related to the question.

definition: A style of software development in which a person describes what they want to an AI and allows the AI to generate and modify much of the code, while the person primarily guides the direction and evaluates whether the result works.
example: I vibe coded the prototype by describing each feature and testing what the AI produced.

definition: A multimodal AI model trained to connect visual information and language so it can perform tasks such as image understanding, captioning, visual question answering, and cross-modal retrieval.
example: The vision-language model examined the diagram and answered questions about what it showed.

definition: Low-effort AI-generated work that appears polished but lacks the context, substance, or judgment needed to be useful, shifting cleanup or thinking work onto the recipient.
example: The report looked finished, but it was workslop: the citations were weak, the analysis missed the actual question, and the reviewer had to redo the thinking.

definition: An application whose primary functionality provides a specialized interface, workflow, or added capabilities around an existing AI model or API.
example: Calling the application a wrapper doesn't necessarily mean it lacks value; the workflow surrounding the model may be the real product.

definition: An AI company founded in 2023 that developed Grok before being acquired by SpaceX in February 2026; its AI services are now presented under SpaceXAI.
example: Older articles may describe Grok as an xAI product, while current official materials identify SpaceXAI as the operator.

definition: Asking an AI to perform a task without first providing examples demonstrating how the task should be completed.
example: The model successfully classified the responses zero-shot.
